question.worked_solution:
First, we find the first-order derivative ${f}_{z}(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{z}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}{z}^{3}\sqrt{y}) \\  & =3{x}^{2}{z}^{2}\sqrt{y}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find ${f}_{zy}(x,y,z)$ by differentiating ${f}_{z}(x,y,z)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{zy}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({f}_{z}(x,y,z)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(3{x}^{2}{z}^{2}\sqrt{y}) \\  & =3{x}^{2}{z}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{y}} \\  & =\frac{3{x}^{2}{z}^{2}}{2\sqrt{y}}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find ${f}_{zyx}(x,y,z)$ by differentiating ${f}_{zy}(x,y,z)$ with respect to $x:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{zyx}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{zy}(x,y,z)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{3{x}^{2}{z}^{2}}{2\sqrt{y}}) \\  & =\frac{3x{z}^{2}}{\sqrt{y}}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we evaluate ${f}_{zyx}(x,y,z)$ at $(2,4,-2):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{zyx}(2,4,-2) & =\frac{3(2)(-2)^{2}}{\sqrt{4}}=\frac{24}{2}=12\end{aligned}
$$
